blocks.task_summary: Find the standard deviation s of a normal distribution with mean 32 given that the interquartile range is 0.28 mm.
method_path: Recognize area below Q1 or above Q3 is 0.25, so P(D < Q1) = 0.25
Obtain inverse normal z-value: z = inv_Phi(0.75) = 0.674489...
Express IQR = Q3 - Q1 = (mu + z*sigma) - (mu - z*sigma) = 2*z*sigma = 0.28
Round to 3 significant figures: sigma = 0.208 mm
accepted_alternatives: Method 1: Compute Q1 = 31.86 and Q3 = 32.14 from IQR = 0.28 and symmetry about mean 32; set up standardised equation (Q3 - 32)/sigma = 0.674489... or (31.86 - 32)/sigma = -0.674489...; solve for sigma = 0.208 mm. Alternative: equate normal CDF to 0.25 or 0.75 directly using GDC.
Method 2: Express Q1 = 32 - 0.674489...*sigma and Q3 = 32 + 0.674489...*sigma; use IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 2 * 0.674489...*sigma = 0.28; solve for sigma = 0.208 mm.

evidence.basis: Q1 = 31.86 OR Q3 = 32.14 (A1); recognition that area under the normal curve below Q1 or above Q3 is 0.25 OR area between Q1 and Q3 is 0.5 (M1); z = -0.674489... OR z = 0.674489... (A1); (31.86-32)/sigma = -0.674489... OR (32.14-32)/sigma = 0.674489... (A1); sigma = 0.207564... approx 0.208 (mm) A1.
